blindSummary:
This country is among the most progressive destinations in its region for trans visitors, with a cleaner documented profile than several of its neighbours. Legal gender recognition is depathologised (no surgery or psychiatric-diagnosis requirement), and a 2022 reform abolished local jurisdiction in the gender-change procedure — reducing involuntary outing through local bureaucracy. Comprehensive anti-discrimination law covers gender identity, same-sex marriage is legal (2022, via the constitutional court), and no far-right party is in government.

No severe traveler-axis incidents surfaced in research: no mob violence against trans people, no trans-tourist rape, no case of police abuse before a regional human-rights court, and no documented foreign-trans-detention case — unlike several neighbours, where documented incidents include a mob attack at a pride event, a tourist rape, a police beating of a queer person, mishandled extradition of a trans foreigner, and a foreign trans woman held in male-detention placement. The main caveats are a far-right youth campaign promoting a binary-sexes message, an underreporting/trust gap in hate-crime reporting, and thinner detention-placement evidence for a small country.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory; general urban crime is very low.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): one of the most progressive countries in its region - comprehensive anti-discrimination law since 2016 (with an equality-principle ombudsman mechanism); the first country in its region to legalise same-sex marriage (2022 constitutional-court ruling; effective January 2023 with joint adoption); legal gender recognition possible but lacks a clear, modern legal framework.
Global LGBT-rights polling platform country profile: composite LGBT-rights perception scores including a global transgender-rights index.

The interior ministry (Oct 2022): terminated local jurisdiction in gender-change procedures - trans people no longer exposed to involuntary disclosure of their trans identity in their local environment; procedures may now take place at any administrative unit; 157 gender reassignments entered in the civil register since 2005 (31 in 2022).

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2024 (covering 2023), chapter on this country: police failed to intervene in attacks around the Pride march and discouraged reporting; a national LGBT advocacy organisation documented 17 cases and a trans advocacy organisation 25 cases of direct bias-motivated speech in 2023; an emergency parliamentary meeting concluded the ministry should adopt a national action plan.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: courts recognised LGBTI asylum seekers' vulnerabilities; a journalist was ruled to have violated the journalists' code for portraying gender reassignment as commercialised and harmful; two opposition parties proposed criminalising 'promotion' of homosexuality/trans identities (up to 3 years) mirroring anti-propaganda laws seen in two other states - swiftly rejected by the government; a magazine special edition pushed anti-trans narratives; one opposition party proposed removing gender-affirming surgery from health coverage.
A foreign government's 2023 human-rights practices report for this country (archived): official assessment including treatment of LGBTI persons.

Research institute's national report (Jan 2025) for a project on enhancing civil-society capacity to support victims of anti-LGBTQI hate crime: this country's legal and political context on anti-LGBTI hate crimes, part of a regionally funded six-country project.

Foreign news outlet (July 2006): this country passed a same-sex marriage law but with restrictions - ceremonies limited to the two partners and a registration official, no friends or relatives, only in a state office; gay and lesbian organisations welcomed the step but criticised the law as 'insufficient'.

Foreign broadsheet with newswire reporting (Dec 2015): the leader of a major global church urged this country's politicians to 'support the family' four days before the referendum on the gay-marriage law adopted by parliament in March - the referendum (later lost) followed a conservative challenge.
blindLocalsOnly: The depathologised legal-gender-recognition regime and the 2022 local-jurisdiction reform are resident-facing administrative law.
blindTangential: Same-sex marriage legal since 2022 — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
